newsitem.title: GERMANY: Suspected would-be guerrillas give up in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Suspected would-be guerrillas give up in Germany.

text.p: Two Germans wanted on charges of attempting to join the left-wing Red Army Faction (RAF) guerrillas have turned themselves in, state prosecutors said on Thursday.

The two, identified only as Corinna K. and Karl-Heinz G., had been living under false names in northern Germany since 1989. They gave themselves up last Friday because Corinna K. was in poor health and they wanted to return to ordinary life.

Prosecutors said the two were suspected of trying to make contact with and join the RAF, formerly the Baader-Meinhof gang, which waged a war of kidnappings and assassinations on the German establishment in the 1970s and 1980s.
The two allegedly plotted terrorist attacks on RAF lines and equipped themselves with weapons, ammunition and stolen papers, prosecutors said.
They were believed to have spied on individuals and companies to look for potential targets, but gave up their campaign and fled into hiding in December 1989 after an accomplice was detained.
The two were initially accused of theft, falsification of documents and arms offences. When these charges lapsed last May, they were accused of attempted membership of a terrorist group.
